budget_items.topic: Possible additional state funding to the district
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the district was notified it may receive additional funds, described by the superintendent as likely but not certain; the committee said it would develop a plan for the money.
The committee confirmed the warrant amount before approving it along with line item transfers.

Dr. Gilson explained the athletic revolving account had been deeply in deficit and was brought back toward zero through reclassifying charges into local budget lines rather than through revenue growth.

budget_items.topic: Special education transportation open purchase orders
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff noted some open encumbrances were budgeted increases for special ed transportation while at least one was a new, unbudgeted cost, both being carried open pending invoices.
A donor's sister described her late brother's will leaving funds to Lunenburg for a scholarship, which the committee voted to accept.
The donor's sister said the scholarship had previously been given to about 12 students in varying amounts.
A committee member cited another district's low, near-universal-participation DC trip fee as a benchmark while pushing to make Lunenburg's DC trip more affordable or fully funded.

budget_items.topic: FY26 school budget baseline (excluding free cash)
budget_items.what_was_said: Dr. Gilson presented the current FY26 school budget total, not including the separate free cash amount, as the baseline for forward projections.
Rolling the FY26 budget forward produced projected level-services totals for FY27 and FY28, each representing a large increase over the prior year.
The projected increase from FY26 to FY27 was described as a large gap the town would need to close.

budget_items.topic: Assumed new town revenue for FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: Assuming the town could again provide a similar increase in new revenue as prior years, the committee still projected a large remaining budget gap requiring cuts.
The projected increase from FY27 to FY28 was described as another significant gap.

Dr. Gilson said her projections assumed a modest across-the-board increase for supplies while level-funding special education, technology and facilities lines because those costs are too volatile to project.
Dr. Gilson relayed a DESE briefing that federal grants such as Title II/III used for mentoring and EL programming could be cut or bundled starting FY27.
Dr. Gilson said out-of-district tuition costs had risen substantially in recent years, citing a post-COVID spike followed by continued growth.

A committee member pressed to isolate health insurance's share of the projected increase so the public understands it as a cost outside the district's control; a 15% increase on the current health line was estimated.

budget_items.topic: Health insurance line shortfall this year
budget_items.what_was_said: Dr. Gilson said the health insurance line had run short and required a line item transfer to cover it.

budget_items.topic: Revenue needed via CPA versus override
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member argued CPA-funded capital projects (Ritter building, Marshall Park, Turkey Hill) could free up town funds for schools, offsetting some but likely not all of the projected gap.
A committee member described how a town could vote a larger override amount but phase in the tax increase over two years rather than taking it all at once.

minutes.headline: Committee got dire FY27–FY28 budget forecasts and agreed to push for an override or other new revenue.
minutes.summary: This meeting was largely a retirement send-off for outgoing Superintendent Dr. Kate Burnham, with extended public and staff tributes, alongside routine year-end business (transfers, surplus declarations, a scholarship gift, and a preschool/special-education compliance update). The substantive policy work was a first look at FY27 and FY28 budget projections showing large multi-million-dollar gaps, leading the committee to approve a statement for upcoming tri-board meetings committing to seek an override and/or other revenue sources (including discussion of the Community Preservation Act) rather than accept cuts alone.

what_happened.line: The committee accepted FY27 and FY28 projections showing gaps large enough to commit to seeking an override or other new revenue rather than cuts alone.
The committee approved a joint statement for the tri-board process naming that override-or-revenue approach as its position.
The committee voted to restore fifth-grade band only as a fee-funded before/after-school club, not during the school day.
Routine year-end business also passed: FY25 transfers, an encumbrance carryover into FY26, a surplus declaration, and a scholarship gift.
The first tri-board meeting was set for July 8 at 7pm.

why_it_matters: Residents will eventually be asked to vote on an override or other new revenue source; this meeting set that as the committee's negotiating position going into the tri-board process, not a final decision.
The band restoration approach shows one program cut being addressed through a family-paid fee rather than restored school-day funding, which affects who can access it.
The FY27-FY28 gap sets the scale of what cuts or new revenue the town will be weighing in the coming budget cycle.
